title: How Do You Preach a Sermon That Actually Lands?
subtitle: On delivery, application, and the difference between a lecture about the Bible and a word from God to this room

sections.kicker: What You Are Doing Up There
sections.title: A Word, Not a Lecture
sections.body:
You can be entirely correct and entirely useless. You can exegete the passage flawlessly, get the Greek right, organize three clean points, and put a room full of people to sleep with the truth that should have set them on fire.

This is the difference that decides everything. A lecture about the Bible is not the same as a word from God.

A lecture informs. A word confronts, comforts, summons, wounds, heals. The congregation did not gather to learn facts about an ancient text. They came, most of them barely knowing it, hoping that God might actually speak, that the living voice would break through the fog of their week and meet them. Preaching is not a class. It is an event, a thing God does through a man who has been gripped by the text before he ever opens his mouth. I have given lectures dressed as sermons, technically sound and spiritually inert, and I knew it while I was doing it. The room was polite. Nothing happened. Correct is not the goal. Correct is the floor.

sections.title: Preach to This Room
sections.body:
A sermon is not preached to everyone. It is preached to these people, in this room, on this morning, and the preacher who forgets that preaches into the air over their heads.

Know who is in front of you. The marriage on the edge. The grief in the third pew. The doubt no one has said out loud.

You cannot do this from a study alone. You do it because you have been in their homes, in their hospital rooms, in the hard conversations all week, and you carry their actual faces into the pulpit. The pastor who has done the unglamorous work of presence preaches differently, because he is not addressing an abstraction called the congregation. He is speaking to people whose burdens he has felt the weight of. Anticipate the objection the skeptic is forming. Speak to the wound the sufferer brought in. Name the sin the comfortable came in to avoid. A word from God lands because it finds the specific person where they actually are, and the preacher who knows his people can aim. The one who only knows his text fires blind and wonders why nothing falls.

sections.title: The Body and the Voice
sections.body:
How you say it is not separate from what you say. The truth came to us through a Word made flesh, and your flesh is the instrument the next word travels through, so do not despise the craft of delivery as if it were beneath the message.

Preach like you believe it. If the resurrection does not move your voice, why would it move theirs.

Look at them. Get your eyes off the manuscript and onto faces, because the connection that carries a sermon happens through the eyes and dies the moment you bury your head in your notes. Let your voice do what the text does, drop to a whisper where the text is tender, rise where it thunders, slow down and let silence fall where the weight needs room to settle. The pause is one of the most powerful tools you own and the one most preachers are too nervous to use. Do not perform emotion you do not feel, because the room can smell a fake, but do not strangle the emotion you do feel in the name of dignity. Vary the pace. Cut the filler. And above all, get out from behind the wall of your notes, because a man reading a paper at people is not preaching, he is reciting, and the fire that was in the study has gone out somewhere between the page and the pew.

sections.title: Application That Costs Something
sections.body:
The sermon has to land somewhere, and the place it lands is the test of whether it was a word or a lecture. But beware the cheap landing, the application that asks nothing real.

Do not end with be nicer and try harder. That is law with no power, and it leaves the crushed more crushed.

Real application is specific and it costs something. It does not float at the level of be more loving. It says, this week, go to the brother you have not spoken to in two years. It names the actual thing, the actual Tuesday, the actual fear. And real application always runs through the gospel, never around it, because if you only tell people what to do you have handed them a weight and no strength to lift it. Tell them what God has done first, and let the doing flow from the done. Aim for the will and the affections, not just the intellect, because a sermon that only informs the mind changes a person about as much as a weather report. The point was never that they understood. The point was that something moved, that a heart turned, that a person walked out under a Word they cannot now un-hear.

sections.title: The One Thing You Cannot Do
sections.body:
Here is the humbling center of it. You can do everything right, the study, the structure, the delivery, the application, and still nothing happens, because the one thing that makes a sermon a word from God is the one thing entirely outside your control.

You cannot make the Word land. Only the Spirit does that.

This should free you and it should drive you to your knees. It frees you because the salvation of the room was never on your shoulders, and the man who thinks his eloquence converts people is carrying a weight that will crush him and a pride that will ruin him. It drives you to your knees because no amount of craft can substitute for the prayer that precedes the pulpit. So do all the work, every bit of it, refuse the laziness that calls itself trusting God. And then, having done all the work, get on your knees and admit that the work cannot do the thing, that only God speaking through you can turn a dead heart toward him. Preach as if it all depends on you. Pray because you know it does not. The Word that made the world is the Word you are handling, and it has never once needed your help to do what only it can do. Your job is faithfulness. The landing belongs to God.
